name: cli-init-minimal-seed
body: Minimal init seed (built-in starter deck): in the built-in starter-deck branch (no path and no configured default, or `--local` — init-library-resolution), `kalide init` writes, in addition to the deck (`kalide.yaml`, `slides/`, empty `assets/`), a minimal local `templates/` directory: `library.yaml`, ONE slide template `templates/slides/hello/` (a required `title` text field, optional body; a plain layout) with a validating `example.md`, and ONE theme `default` whose `theme.css` uses only system fonts and neutral colours. Its template content is exactly that one slide template and one theme: no sections templates, no fonts, no logos, no media. The deck has one slide `slides/1-hello.md` using `hello`, and `kalide.yaml` has a title and no/`default` theme. The seed is the only template content carried by the binary; it is embedded in internal/scaffold, not internal/assets (global.constraint.no-embedded-template-assets). It is distinct from the richer demo project (demo-project). When the external-library branch is chosen instead (an explicit path, or the configured default — init-library-resolution), `kalide init` does not use this seed at all: it writes no local `templates/` and no starter slide, and the external library's template names are unconstrained — a valid external library need define no template (see cli-init, external-template-library). The seed init also writes the deck guide pair (agent-authoring, agent-guide-reference): the project-root full guide `AGENTS_KALIDE.md`, verbatim from the static file embedded in internal/scaffold, written when absent, and the project-root `AGENTS.md` pointer that carries the line `Kalide Reference: ./AGENTS_KALIDE.md` — created carrying the embedded pointer content (agent-guide-reference) when absent, left byte-for-byte untouched when it already contains the string, and otherwise appended to with the reference line while the author content is byte-preserved. Both are text-only, not template assets and never read by validate/render/serve/list. AC: immediately after a seed init, `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` and a referencing `AGENTS.md` exist at the project root, and `kalide start` validates templates and deck cleanly and serves the single "hello world" slide.
